subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Identifiable Victim Effect
description: A quick win: understand The Identifiable Victim Effect.

hook.text: A fundraiser for one named girl raised more than a campaign for millions of unnamed famine victims.

buildup.text: Small and Loewenstein found that a single identified victim triggers more giving than statistical victims.

discovery.text: The identifiable victim effect: we respond to faces and stories, not to numbers. One life outweighs millions.

twist.text: Adding statistics to the individual's story actually reduces donations. Numbers dilute the emotional pull.

climax.text: Charities learned this: lead with one person's story. The brain gives to people, not to percentages.

punchline.text: One name moves more than a million numbers.

quiz.question: What happens when statistics are added to an individual victim's story?
